newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Foreign aluminium can makers lining up in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Foreign aluminium can makers lining up in Brazil.

text.p: Demand for aluminium cans is expected to more than double in Brazil over the next eight years, prompting foreign can makers to invest heavily here, analysts said.
"Brazil is 20 years behind the times in the use of aluminium cans," said Adjarma Azevedo, president of Brazil's Aluminium Association (ABAL).

U.S. can makers, which became Brazil's first producers of aluminium cans in 1990, have invested $450 million in the country over the last two years to build plants in south-eastern states, the nation's largest market for cans.
These investments are expected to double Brazil's aluminium can output capacity to roughly 8 billion cans by mid-1997, analysts said.
Aluminium can production is projected to jump to 10 billion cans annually by 2004 from the current 4 billion cans.
Reynolds Latasa, a subsidiary of U.S. Reynolds Metals Co, has been Brazil's largest aluminium can producer since 1990 when it opened its factory in Minas Gerais state.
Today, Reynolds Latasa employs 1,000 workers, has an output capacity of 5.4 billion cans annually and recycles more than 1,800 tonnes of aluminium cans.
Earlier this year, another U.S. firm, Crown Cork and Seal Inc, started making cans in Brazil. And others are on the way.
The American National Can (ANC) company and Ball Metals, both of the United States, are planning to inaugurate their first Brazilian plants in February 1997.
Ballooning can production plus a limited number of participants in the market has made recycling aluminium cans a promising niche in Brazil and attracted domestic and foreign interest.
Currently Brazil has only two recycling firms, Reynolds Latasa and Alcan's Brazilian unit.
US IMCO Recycling Inc is studying partnerships with Brazilian firms to build a plant in Brazil, said Richard L. Kerr, IMCO's president.

By early 1997, Brazilian construction group Parizzotto will inaugurate the country's most modern recycling aluminium can plant in Sao Paulo state, known as Recipar, said Ary de Oliveira Filho, Recipar's manager.
The plant will have an output capacity of 20,000 tonnes of aluminium alloys, which will be sold on domestic and international markets.
